correctness.rationale: For every finite nonempty P, chain inequalities imply x^+ and x^- separately satisfy Stanley chain-polytope constraints, and conversely any difference of two chain-polytope points satisfies the two-sided signed-chain inequalities. The exact Minkowski identity follows. Stanley antichain generators then give squared norm |A symmetric_difference B|, bounded by second Greene width with equality at disjoint maximizing antichains. Strict squared-norm convexity excludes every other sphere contact. The antipodal pair proves sharp radius, unique center and diameter. Proper two-colorings of each maximizing induced comparability graph give the exact 2^{components} count. Independent exact standard-library enumerations checked 407 naturally labeled posets, 36,947 integer points, and 3,158 contact occurrences; these finite computations corroborate the symbolic proof only.

value.rationale: The result recovers the classical second Greene--Kleitman k-family size (rather than ordinary width) as an exact Euclidean outer radius of a natural signed-chain polytope, with a complete nontrivial contact-count formula indexed by maximizing two-families and their comparability components. Its sharp ratio to the enriched-chain sphere and explicit contact formulas for chains, antichains and layered posets distinguish two near-named constructions geometrically. This is a natural global classification, not an arbitrary finite slice, renamed theorem or unsupported numerical gain.
